# Remix Agent Guide

This repository includes the source code for Remix 3, a web framework for building modern web applications using TypeScript/JavaScript and web standard APIs.

## Repo Shape

- **Monorepo**: pnpm workspace with most product code under `packages/`
- **Public API layout**: every `exports` entry in `package.json` should map to a dedicated top-level `src/*.ts` file
- **Implementation layout**: `src/lib` is implementation-only; do not add barrel re-exports or thin pass-through wrappers inside `src/lib`
- **Cross-package boundaries**: do not re-export APIs or types from another package; import from the owning package directly
- **Platform stance**: prefer Web APIs and standards-aligned primitives over Node-specific APIs whenever possible

## Default Development Loop

- **Fast local loop**: `pnpm run validate-package-meta`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run test:changed`, `pnpm run typecheck:changed`
- **Full CI-style validation**: `pnpm test` and `pnpm run typecheck`
- **When to use full runs locally**: broad cross-workspace changes, shared root config changes, release/publish flow changes, or anything that could affect the whole repo
- **Single package commands**: `pnpm --filter @remix-run/<package> run test`, `pnpm --filter @remix-run/<package> run typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @remix-run/<package> run build`
- **Single test file**: `cd packages/<package> && pnpm test src/**/<filename>.test.ts`
- **Lint**: `pnpm run lint` or `pnpm run lint:fix`
- **Format**: `pnpm run format` or `pnpm run format:check`

The changed-workspace commands default to diffing against `origin/main` and include uncommitted working tree changes when `head-ref` is `HEAD`.

## Code Style

- **Imports**: use `import type { X }` and `export type { X }`; include `.ts` extensions
- **Variables**: use `let` for locals, `const` for module scope, never `var`
- **Functions**: use regular functions by default; use arrow functions for callbacks; use concise arrow bodies when they only return an expression
- **Object methods**: use shorthand method syntax
- **Classes**: omit TS accessibility modifiers; use native fields and `#private`
- **Generics**: use descriptive lowercase names like `source`, `pattern`, or `method`
- **Comments**: add non-JSDoc comments only when behavior is surprising or non-obvious
- **Formatting**: Prettier with `printWidth: 100`, no semicolons, single quotes, spaces not tabs

## Tests And Docs

- **Tests run from source**: no build step required
- **Test structure**: do not generate tests inside `describe()` with loops or conditionals; it breaks per-test IDE execution
- **Test guidance**: use the `write-tests` skill when adding, refactoring, or reviewing tests, fixtures, test scripts, or test-only dependencies
- **Docs and examples**: if you change a public API, update the related docs, JSDoc, README examples, and tests in the same change
- **README/install conventions**: use `npm i remix` in install snippets and import from `remix`, not `@remix-run/*`
- **README link conventions**: use full GitHub URLs for cross-file or cross-package repo links so copied docs render correctly; keep same-document anchors and README self-links relative

## GitHub

- **GitHub work**: when commenting on issues or pull requests, inspecting GitHub state, or otherwise working with GitHub, always use the `gh` command line tool when possible instead of an agent-specific connector

## Release Notes

- If a change affects published packages, add or update the appropriate change file.
- Prerelease channels come from `packages/*/.changes/config.json` and control the version suffix such as `alpha` or `beta`; prerelease packages still publish to the npm `next` dist-tag.
- If you modify release or publish flow code, validate it with the preview or dry-run scripts before finishing.

## Repo Skills

For work on this repository itself, use the skills in `.agents/skills/`:

- `add-package` at `.agents/skills/add-package/SKILL.md`: Create or align a package under `packages/` with repo conventions.
- `author-ui-modules` at `.agents/skills/author-ui-modules/SKILL.md`: Build idiomatic `packages/ui` modules, including first-party UI primitives, headless controls, and mixin-based modules.
- `fix-issue` at `.agents/skills/fix-issue/SKILL.md`: Fix bugs reported in GitHub issues.
- `make-change-file` at `.agents/skills/make-change-file/SKILL.md`: Create or update package change files under `packages/*/.changes`.
- `make-decision-doc` at `.agents/skills/make-decision-doc/SKILL.md`: Add a numbered decision document under `decisions/` capturing a non-obvious architectural choice.
- `make-demo` at `.agents/skills/make-demo/SKILL.md`: Create or revise demos in this repository with production-quality Remix patterns.
- `make-pr` at `.agents/skills/make-pr/SKILL.md`: Prepare and open clear, reviewer-friendly pull requests.
- `publish-placeholder-package` at `.agents/skills/publish-placeholder-package/SKILL.md`: Publish a `0.0.0` placeholder package to reserve an npm name.
- `review-pr` at `.agents/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md`: Review Remix pull requests from a local checkout.
- `remix` at `.agents/skills/remix/SKILL.md`: Build, review, and refactor Remix apps end to end, including project layout, routes, controllers, middleware, validation, data access, auth, sessions, uploads, UI, hydration, navigation, animations, and tests.
- `supersede-pr` at `.agents/skills/supersede-pr/SKILL.md`: Replace one pull request with another and close the superseded PR safely.
- `typescript-expert` at `.agents/skills/typescript-expert/SKILL.md`: Write, refactor, or review TypeScript with strict, precise, maintainable types.
- `update-pr` at `.agents/skills/update-pr/SKILL.md`: Rewrite an existing pull request title and body to match the current diff.
- `write-api-docs` at `.agents/skills/write-api-docs/SKILL.md`: Write or tighten JSDoc for exported public APIs.
- `write-readme` at `.agents/skills/write-readme/SKILL.md`: Draft or revise package READMEs in the repo's style.
- `write-tests` at `.agents/skills/write-tests/SKILL.md`: Write, refactor, or review tests with repo runner, fixture, assertion, dependency, and validation conventions.
- `write-ui-module-readme` at `.agents/skills/write-ui-module-readme/SKILL.md`: Write concise module README files for `packages/ui/src/lib/*` primitives.

## App And Demo Skills

For working on Remix code in demos or writing Remix app code, use the root `remix` skill listed above.

The CLI prepack step copies `.agents/skills/remix` into the default app template so scaffolded apps can refer to `./.agents/skills/remix/SKILL.md`.

---
name: project-uriel-canon
description: Canon rules for the IceBerg project — Uriel's angelic classification system and character details
metadata:
  type: project
---

## Angelic ranking system (two-axis)

**Power axis** (strongest → weakest):
Seraph > Throne > Dominion > Cherub > Archangel > Paedorium

*Paedorium* — invented term from Latin *paedor* (dirt); represents angels closest to humanity.

**Job axis** (role, independent of power):
- Grigori — Watchers
- Malakhim — Messengers
- Virtues — embodiments of divine attributes

Power class defines strength; job axis defines function. They are independent.

## Uriel

- **Power class**: Throne (second highest)
- **Former role**: Grigori (one of the good ones — no longer active as a Watcher)
- **Virtue**: Wisdom and Judgement
- **Realm**: Eden, Third Heaven
- **Why:** "Archangel of Wisdom" is WRONG — Archangel is a lower power class than Throne. Never call Uriel an Archangel.

**How to apply:** Always label Uriel as "Throne class" in UI copy. Reference the job axis separately (former Grigori, current Virtue of Wisdom and Judgement). Do not conflate the two axes.

there are Two Timelines for her
Here is a structured, in-universe description of Uriel across both timelines, based *only* on the content of the four books you shared. No meta-commentary, no authorial self-insertion, no information from our conversation outside the texts.

---

## TIMELINE A: *Book of Beginnings* → *Book of Exile*

### Origin & Creation
Uriel is created by YHWH and Lucifer together as the fourth of the firstborn angels. Lucifer shapes her with precision: *Observer, Recorder, Neutral*. These words are woven into her sinew as her fundamental purpose. Her eyes are blue—the blue of deep water, of the space between stars. She is tall, still, unreadable. She does not smile.

Her function is the archive. She moves through facets of frozen light, recording human deeds with perfect fidelity. She feels nothing—or almost nothing. A small, warm pressure lives somewhere in her marrow, in a place Lucifer's design did not reach. She does not name it. She does not know she can.

### The Gap
Over centuries of watching humanity, Uriel notices a flaw in the archive: it records actions but not *why*. A woman shares her bread—the archive shows the act, but not her reasoning. A man steals—the archive shows the theft, but not his hunger or desperation. The missing interior, the slow process by which a soul becomes itself, is absent. Uriel cannot file incomplete records. Her hand refuses to close around a facet that lacks the *why*. She sets it aside, unresolved.

She attends the council where YHWH and Lucifer debate free will. YHWH argues for love that must be chosen. Lucifer argues for order without suffering. Neither asks what humans actually *need*. Uriel stands at the edge, silent, but she names the gap: *education*. Free will without instruction is cruelty. She does not speak. She needs to be certain first.

### The Proposal & The Garden
Uriel proposes the Grigori mission: angels stationed on Earth to observe and report, filling what the archive cannot hold. It is never approved.

She is sent to guard the gate of Eden. She stands at the threshold, watching Adam and Eve. Eve, in particular, draws her attention—the way she looks at the forbidden tree, not with hunger but with questions. *Why is this one forbidden? What is on the other side?* Uriel recognizes herself in Eve's questioning. The small, warm pressure in her chest becomes recognition.

### The Judgment & After
Uriel does not interfere. The Fall happens without her direct intervention. After the exile, YHWH expands the heavenly bureaucracy. Uriel is elevated: she receives a flaming sword and becomes the Guardian of Eden's gate. She is no longer merely a recorder—she is a *judge*. Her eyes remain blue. She stands at the gate of paradise, determining which souls are worthy to enter. She judges without cruelty, without mercy, without attachment. The system works.

When Cain kills Abel, Uriel descends to pronounce judgment. She sees everything: Cain's years of watching, his certainty that Abel was favored, the moment by the stream, the knife, Abel's dying question—*why?* She tells Cain the truth: there was no chosen. God does not speak in the silence. The peace on Abel's face was not favor—it was contentment. Cain mistook ease for election.

She curses Cain: the ground will not yield for him. He will be a fugitive and a wanderer. But she does not kill him. She marks him for protection and lets him walk away.

She tells Eve that Abel is home. At peace. With the One who made him.

He chooses to die.

### The Murder & After
Cain kills Abel by the stream. Uriel feels it—the thread of Abel's presence going slack, like a candle going out. She does not scream. She walks to the meadow. She kneels beside him. She holds his hand.

She does not kill Cain. She knows YHWH will handle it.

She returns to the settlement. She holds Ariel and John. She does not explain. They are too young to understand.

### The Twins
Weeks later, Uriel discovers she is pregnant. The twins were conceived before Abel's death. He never knew. She carries them through her grief, names them alone: Noxiel (Darkness of God) and Sariel (Strength of God). She gives birth in the spring. Ariel meets her new brothers. John touches their tiny faces. Uriel sits in the darkness with all four children and begins the long work of raising them without him.

Uriel is a widow. A mother of four. A fallen angel. A former Throne, now Archangel-rank but outside the system entirely. She has no function. No title. No rules binding her.

She has grief. She has children. She has the memory of a shepherd who found her in the forest and loved her until death.

She does not know what she will become. She only knows she will keep going.

For them. For him. For all of it.

# URIEL: COMPLETE IN-UNIVERSE PROFILE

## PART ONE: ORIGIN & NATURE (Both Timelines)

### Creation
Uriel is created by YHWH and Lucifer together as the fourth of the firstborn angels. Lucifer shapes her with precision, weaving three words into her sinew: *Observer. Recorder. Neutral.* Her purpose is to watch, to document, to remain detached. Her eyes are blue—the blue of deep water, of the space between stars. She is tall, still, unreadable. She does not smile.

YHWH's warmth brushes against her during creation, softening the edges of Lucifer's design. Something small and warm lives in Uriel's marrow, in a place Lucifer did not think to reach. She does not name it. She does not know she can.

### The Archive
Uriel's function is the archive—a realm of facets of frozen light where human deeds are recorded. She moves through them without sound, without touch, cataloguing actions with perfect fidelity. A man helps his neighbor. Filed. A woman shares her bread. Filed. A child defends a smaller child. Filed.

But the archive records only *what* happens, not *why*. The interior of human reasoning—the slow, circuitous process by which a soul becomes itself—is absent. Uriel cannot file incomplete records. Her hand refuses to close around a facet that lacks the *why*. She sets it aside, unresolved.

### The Small, Warm Pressure
From her earliest moments, Uriel feels something beneath her function—a pulse behind her ribs, the faintest sensation of something that feels almost like care. She feels it at Cain's birth, watching Eve hold her firstborn. She feels it watching a child share bread with a stranger. She feels it watching a man strike his wife—not warmth, but coldness. A tightness. The sense that something is wrong.

The archive has no category for wrongness. She files the observation anyway.

### The Gap
Uriel notices that Heaven's observation of humanity captures actions but not their interior. The archive records that a man helped his neighbor. It does not record the hesitation before the helping, the calculus of cost and risk, the small internal victory of choosing generosity over self-preservation.

She names the gap: *why*. The missing interior. The space where a soul's reasoning lives.

- **Raphael** — healing requires intervention. His first instinct when confronted with suffering is to mend. Glorious—and catastrophic for a mission defined by non-interference.
- **Michael** — absurd. His presence on Earth would terrify any human within a mile.

Uriel recognizes her own capability. She understands duration. She has guarded Eden's gate for centuries. She has rendered judgment on Cain, delivered warnings to Noah. She has never flinched, never softened, never exceeded her mandate. She is the correct instrument for this function.

She never receives approval to deploy the mission. The Grigori do not exist in Timeline A.

### The Council
YHWH and Lucifer debate free will. YHWH argues for love that must be chosen. Lucifer argues for order without suffering. Neither asks what humans actually need. Uriel stands at the edge, silent, but she knows the variable is not control or freedom—it is *instruction*. Free will without teaching is cruelty.

- She becomes the **Guardian of Eden's gate** , judging which souls are worthy to enter the reborn paradise.
- She is appointed one of the five **Stewards** of Heaven, alongside Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Metatron.
- She receives a **Virtue** : Temperance (or Justice—the text is ambiguous). She is the arbiter of what is right.

When Cain kills Abel, Uriel descends to pronounce judgment. She sees everything: Cain's years of watching, his certainty that Abel was favored, the moment by the stream, the knife, Abel's dying question—*why?*

She curses Cain: the ground will not yield for him. He will be a fugitive and a wanderer, marked by what he has done, forever moving, forever alone. But she does not kill him. She marks him for protection and lets him walk away.

She tells Eve that Abel is home. At peace. With the One who made him.

## Uriel

- **Power class**: Throne (second highest) — demoted to Archangel-rank in Timeline B after the Fall
- **Former role**: Grigori (one of the good ones); assembled the Grigori team (Metatron proposed the mission, Uriel was to lead it)
- **Virtue**: Wisdom and Judgement (Timeline A: also Temperance/Justice — text ambiguous)
- **Realm**: Eden, Third Heaven (Timeline A); periphery / mortal world (Timeline B)
- **Eyes**: Blue (Timeline A) / Green (Timeline B — mark of her choice in the garden)
- **Weapon**: Flaming sword (Timeline A, kept); taken from her in Timeline B's judgment
- **Why:** "Archangel of Wisdom" is WRONG — Archangel is a lower power class than Throne. Never call Uriel an Archangel (except noting her demotion in Timeline B).

**How to apply:** Always label Uriel as "Throne class" in UI copy. Reference the job axis separately. Do not conflate the two axes.

## Key characters & connections

### YHWH
- Co-creator of Uriel (with Lucifer)
- Timeline A: Uriel serves her as judge/Guardian without question; YHWH withdraws after Cain's murder
- Timeline B: Judges and exiles Uriel after Eden; their eyes meet after judgment — warmth, recognition, not forgiveness

### Lucifer
- Co-creator of Uriel; shaped her function (Observer. Recorder. Neutral.)
- Timeline A: No significant interaction after the council
- Timeline B: Recruits Uriel for the war; she agrees conditionally (humans must survive); does not save her when she falls

### Metatron
- Fellow Steward of Heaven; Keeper of the Akashic Records
- Proposed the Grigori mission (Timeline A — never approved; Timeline B — Uriel acts instead)

### Michael
- Fellow Steward (Fortitude and Justice)
- Timeline A: serve together, not close
- Timeline B: enemies on the battlefield; wounds Uriel (or she wounds him — text unclear)

### Gabriel
- Fellow Steward (Faith and Kindness)
- Timeline B: carries Lucifer's message to Hell; tells Lucifer about Uriel's judgment; no direct interaction with Uriel

### Raphael
- Fellow Steward (Temperance and Healing)
- No direct connection in Timeline B

### Abel (Timeline B only)
- Husband; finds Uriel broken in the forest, asks nothing, gives bread and water
- Thanks her for teaching Eve ("You're the reason I exist at all")
- Chooses to die rather than break the fixed point; never knows about the twins
- Father of Ariel, John, Noxiel, Sariel

### Eve
- Timeline A: Uriel watches her at the gate, recognises herself in Eve's questioning; does not intervene
- Timeline B: Uriel teaches her as the Green Vine Snake; Eve recognises her later, thanks her — "Daughters do what they must. Even when it costs them everything."

### Cain
- Timeline A: Uriel pronounces judgment — curses him (ground will not yield, fugitive and wanderer), marks him for protection, does not kill him
- Timeline B: brother-in-law; kills Abel; Uriel does not kill him, trusts YHWH

### Adam (Timeline B)
- Father-in-law; accepts Uriel into the settlement — "If he brought you here, you belong here."

### Uriel's children (Timeline B only)
- **Ariel** — daughter, firstborn, Lion of God; watches everything, stillness like her mother
- **John** — son, God is gracious; most human name; too young to remember Abel
- **Noxiel** — son (twin), Darkness of God; born after Abel's death, conceived before; named for the grief Uriel carries
- **Sariel** — son (twin), Strength of God; born after Abel's death, conceived before; loud, demanding; named for what Uriel needs to become
